title: JASSM/LRASM resources are accompanied by reported production-capacity and integration milestones
source_unit: Lockheed Martin corporate program announcements, with a contemporaneous US Department of Defense contract notice as a corroborative contract-stage source
geography: United States; Lockheed Martin and DoD work locations reported in Orlando, Florida and the US production base

observations.period: FY2026 Air Force Missile Procurement Exhibit P-21, June 2025; official SAF/FM document checked September 18, 2026

denominator.unit: official Air Force JASSM/LRASM production-schedule exhibit

combined_minimum_sustained_rate.unit: missiles per year; JASSM and LRASM combined FY2026 minimum sustained rate

jassm_minimum_sustained_rate.unit: missiles per year; JASSM allocation within shared FY2026 production rate

lrasm_capacity_allocation.unit: missiles per year; LRASM allocation within shared FY2026 production rate

capacity_change_reason.value: minimum sustained rate increased due to a new operational production facility

accepted_output_and_customer_delivery.unit: missing accepted quantity, shipment, delivery, fielding, and inventory endpoint

observations.method: Official Air Force budget-exhibit extraction via the SAF/FM FY2026 missile-procurement document; the shared production rate, variant allocation, manufacturer/location, and stated capacity-change reason are kept separate from delivered or accepted output.
observations.uncertainty: The exhibit reports a planned/minimum sustained production rate and shared-line allocation, not realized FY2026 throughput, lot acceptance, delivery timing, inventory, staffing, yield, or facility-specific assignment of a customer order. The local command-line PDF retrieval returned a TLS error, so the exhibit is retained from official indexed/web access without a repository copy.
observations.subgroup: Lockheed Martin Troy production site, JASSM and LRASM program offices, Air Force procurement, US and foreign military customers, production workers, and suppliers sharing the line.
observations.counterinterpretation: A higher minimum sustained rate and new facility can expand potential replenishment capacity while bottlenecks, variant mix, testing, acceptance, customer priority, or supply constraints limit delivered operational inventory.

reported_capacity_action.value: contract award to increase JASSM/LRASM production capacity

reported_new_factory_size.unit: square feet; facility brought online in 2022 according to announcement

observations.method: Qualitative extraction from a dated Lockheed Martin program announcement; the capacity action is kept separate from realized output or delivery counts.
observations.uncertainty: The announcement does not provide missile quantities produced, accepted, delivered, staffing, throughput, yield, or facility-specific output. It is a corporate source and includes forward-looking claims.
observations.subgroup: JASSM and LRASM large-lot production program and associated US production infrastructure.
observations.counterinterpretation: A capacity investment or production-support award can coexist with bottlenecks, schedule slippage, input constraints, or no near-term increase in accepted inventory.

integration_test_event.value: initial flight test integrating LRASM onto the F-35B

test_location.value: Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland

observations.method: Dated Lockheed Martin newsroom report describing the event and its test-program position; treated as an integration milestone, not a fielding or acceptance result.
observations.uncertainty: The event establishes a reported flight test, but not successful completion of the full test program, certification, production delivery, operational deployment, combat performance, or changed adversary/alliance behavior.
observations.subgroup: LRASM weapon system integration with the F-35B platform within the broader AGM-158 family.
observations.counterinterpretation: A flight test can identify integration or software/hardware issues and may precede substantial additional testing before operational use.

loaded_missile_test.unit: AGM-158 missiles loaded on external stations during the described two-day test

test_location.value: Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland

observations.method: Government-published DVIDS image record and caption describing an F-35C flight test and the Pax River F-35 Integrated Test Force mission; treated as an independent test-event corroboration.
observations.uncertainty: The record documents a test event and its stated evaluation dimensions, not certification completion, production acceptance, delivery, fleet fielding, or combat effectiveness.
observations.subgroup: AGM-158C LRASM integration with the F-35C carrier variant, within a test program covering F-35B and F-35C variants.
observations.counterinterpretation: Flight testing is an intermediate verification/certification step and may surface issues or require additional tests before operational use.

related_sources.claim: DoD contract notice dated 2024-09-27 reports a $3.230B firm-fixed-price undefinitized action for JASSM Lot 22 and FMS missiles, with Orlando performance and completion expected July 31, 2032.
related_sources.access_boundary: Official page was available through indexed/web retrieval but returned HTTP 403 to the local command-line fetch during this pass; the claim is retained as corroborative context, not as a locally hashed raw artifact.

boundary: This record establishes reported capacity, production-support, and integration-test milestones for one US weapons program. It does not establish missile output, delivery, acceptance, inventory, operational readiness, workforce or local incidence, resilience, deterrence, leverage, or an external actor's changed behavior.
